events.title: FOMC minutes (Sept 15–16 hike to 3.75–4.00%)
events.why_it_matters: Minutes drop at 14:00 ET for a unanimous 25 bp hike whose dots still implied one more 2026 move, but they predate the +29k NFP miss that crushed October hike odds to ~20%.
events.what_to_watch: Whether 'most' vs 'several' wanted more hikes, any hidden dissent, and how they weighed inflation persistence versus a cooling labor market.

events.title: US–Iran war: Hormuz still restricted; Iran's 7 conditions unmet
events.why_it_matters: Seven-month war plus a contested Strait of Hormuz remains the regime-level oil, shipping, diesel, and inflation premium in global risk assets.
events.what_to_watch: Any post–Camp David military step, tanker incidents, and whether AIS crossings stay ~10% of normal versus US claims of recovered crude flows.

events.title: Brent ~$101: crude transits rebound, refined products still tight
events.why_it_matters: Crude exports through Hormuz have recovered toward ~prewar ~13.5 mb/d, but diesel/gasoline flows, tanker rates, and insurance keep a consumer-tax and CPI input in place.
events.what_to_watch: Brent holding $100, US diesel, and whether product tightness fades as escorts/bypasses scale.

events.title: China Golden Week (National Day) last day: travel vs spend
events.why_it_matters: Early prints show huge trip volume (~782m domestic trips) but still-cautious per-capita spend — the live read on whether property-scarred households are thawing.
events.what_to_watch: Official holiday tourism/retail wrap after Oct 7 and how mainland equities gap on the Oct 8 reopen.

events.title: Southern California record October heat / wildfire overlay
events.why_it_matters: Record SoCal October heat lifts power demand and fire risk into SEMICON West week; Bouquet Fire ~1k acres is contained enough not to be a national disaster tape.
events.what_to_watch: Heat warnings through Oct 8, CAISO load, and any red-flag wind shift.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure vs silicon shield (no invasion base case)
events.why_it_matters: Coast-guard/quarantine tactics and cable-adjacent research vessels are the slow-burn risk to TSMC power/shipping, not an imminent invasion.
events.what_to_watch: Cable-patrol incidents, ADIZ tempo, and any TSMC commentary around the Oct 15 print.

events.title: US Gulf carrier buildup after Camp David Iran 'war council'
events.why_it_matters: Vance-chaired Oct 2–3 Camp David session plus a reported path to three carriers / ~20k personnel by late October raises odds of a kinetic or sanctions step before Nov 3 midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Carrier arrivals, CENTCOM strikes, and any White House readout tying Iran to the midterm clock.

events.title: September NFP miss: +29k, U3 4.2%, wages +3.0% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Payrolls badly missed ~+90k, prior months revised −60k, wages slowed — collapsing October FOMC hike odds to ~17–22% while leaving a growth-scare tail.
events.what_to_watch: Whether CPI (Oct 14) and retail sales (Oct 15) confirm demand destruction or just a hiring freeze.

events.title: Eurozone September flash HICP 3.8% y/y (energy spike)
events.why_it_matters: Hottest headline since 2023, energy ~18.8% y/y, tests the ECB's post–Sept 10 25 bp hike 'hold' into the Oct 29 meeting (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: Oct 16 final HICP confirmation and whether core stays ~2.5%.

events.title: OPEC+ holds November output targets unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Core producers paused after finishing the 1.65 mb/d unwind; actual barrels remain below quotas because of the Iran war, so the signal is 'no extra supply'.
events.what_to_watch: Next core-group review Nov 1 (outside window); compliance vs war-lost barrels.

events.title: Camp David Iran war council after Hormuz rejection
events.why_it_matters: Senior US principals met with no public readout as Iran restated Hormuz stays shut until seven conditions are met.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through via the carrier buildup and any new OFAC/military action this window.

events.title: Tokyo September core CPI +2.7% y/y (hot lead for national CPI)
events.why_it_matters: Well above ~2.1–2.3% consensus after BoJ's Sept hike to 1.25%, keeping another hike in play at the Oct 29–30 meeting (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: National CPI due Oct 23 and Ueda's 'underlying inflation at 2%' Outlook-report language.

events.title: US August goods-and-services trade deficit $105.6bn
events.why_it_matters: Widest deficit since March 2025 as imports hit a record $420.8bn — a read on tariff-front-running plus the oil import bill after the truce extension.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Q3 GDP (Oct 29, outside window) is dragged by net exports.

events.title: ISM Services PMI 54.9; prices paid 74.0
events.why_it_matters: Activity still expanding after the NFP miss, but prices paid at 74.0 (highest since July 2022) keeps the stagflation/oil-pass-through narrative alive.
events.what_to_watch: CPI services and PPI pipeline into the Oct 14–15 prints.

events.title: Emergency diesel excise-tax deferral EO
events.why_it_matters: White House directed Treasury to defer diesel excise taxes Oct 5–Dec 31 and ease dyed-diesel penalties — an admission that product tightness is a political problem into midterms.
events.what_to_watch: IRS guidance within 5 days, state copycat relief, and whether pump diesel actually eases.

events.title: US–China Busan truce extended to Jan 10, 2027
events.why_it_matters: Bessent/Xi extension pushed the Nov 10 cliff to Jan 10 2027, pausing reciprocal-tariff snapbacks, some 301 exclusions, ship fees, and China rare-earth controls.
events.what_to_watch: Whether USTR actually publishes the Federal Register notices; some ship-fee/exclusion clocks still cited as Nov 9.

events.title: US–China $60bn '30-for-30' non-sensitive tariff-cut lists
events.why_it_matters: Reciprocal ~$30bn lists (toys/housewares vs ag/coal/timber/med-devices) cut the near-term China tariff cliff without touching semis, EVs, or critical minerals.
events.what_to_watch: Domestic implementation timing; soybeans were notably excluded from China's list.

events.title: FCC unlocks >1 GHz satellite/wireless spectrum (Sept 30)
events.why_it_matters: 12.7–13.25 and 42–42.5 GHz FSS allocations plus thinner NEPA reviews are a structural positive for satellite broadband and wireless capex.
events.what_to_watch: License/implementation timeline and competitive response from terrestrial 5G vs LEO operators.

events.title: Graham Act: USTR/President notice then secondary-tariff clock
events.why_it_matters: Statutory up-to-100% secondary tariffs on top-5 Russian-energy buyers/evasion facilitators (China/India first) stack on 301/232; up-to-500% on Russian-origin goods.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 8 congressional justification, Oct 18 (Sunday → likely Oct 17/20) country list and rates, and any India-deal waiver.

events.title: China mainland markets reopen after Golden Week
events.why_it_matters: First onshore price discovery after a week of Hormuz, NFP, and Graham-Act headlines while HK/offshore traded.
events.what_to_watch: A-share gap, CNY, and property/consumer names vs holiday spend prints.

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: First mega-cap staples print of Q3 season — pricing power vs $100 oil and a cooling US consumer after the NFP miss.
events.what_to_watch: Volume vs price mix, Frito-Lay margins, and FY guidance.

events.title: Samsung Electronics Q3 2026 preliminary results
events.why_it_matters: Street is looking for record OP ~₩108–111tn on AI memory/HBM — the Korea-side confirmation of the Micron boom into SEMICON West/ASML/TSMC week.
events.what_to_watch: DRAM/HBM commentary and whether guidance implies 2027 still tighter than 2026.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Q3 2026 earnings (jet-fuel stress test)
events.why_it_matters: Bellwether airline vs Brent >$100; Q3 plan assumed jet fuel far below wartime peaks, so CASM-ex and 4Q guide are the tell for travel demand.
events.what_to_watch: Fuel hedge/guide, domestic unit revenue, and any capacity cuts.

events.title: US bank Q3 open: JPM, GS, C, WFC (13th); BAC, MS (14th)
events.why_it_matters: NII, credit, and trading vs a 10y near multi-decade highs and a labor miss — the first hard read on whether the growth scare is in loan books.
events.what_to_watch: Net interest margin, charge-offs, capital-markets revenue, and CEOs on the consumer.

events.title: UnitedHealth Group Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Healthcare bellwether on medical-cost trend and Medicare Advantage — a sector-wide multiple reset if utilization stays hot.
events.what_to_watch: MLR, MA membership, and 2027 preliminary view.

events.title: SEMICON West 2026 (San Francisco)
events.why_it_matters: Industry gathering as AI-memory tightness is already validated by Micron/Korea; tool/capex talk will be read against ASML/TSMC the same week.
events.what_to_watch: WFE/HBM capacity comments and any China-export-control color.

events.title: China September CPI and PPI
events.why_it_matters: First official inflation after Golden Week; street PPI around ~4.5% y/y on energy while CPI still tests whether domestic demand is thawing.
events.what_to_watch: Core CPI vs food/energy split and any PBoC follow-through after holiday liquidity.

events.title: US September CPI (headline energy vs core)
events.why_it_matters: Consensus clusters ~+0.5–0.6% m/m headline / +0.2% core (~3.6–3.7% / 2.4% y/y); a hot headline from gasoline can reprice December hike odds after NFP killed October.
events.what_to_watch: Core services, gasoline contribution, and whether markets fade headline for core.

events.title: ASML Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: WFE/EUV bellwether for the AI capex cycle; booked against SEMICON West and TSMC the next morning.
events.what_to_watch: 2027 backlog, China shipments, and High-NA commentary.

events.title: September PPI and advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: PPI is the pipeline into CPI/PCE after ISM services prices at 74; retail sales test whether $100 oil is already destroying goods demand after the NFP miss.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI, control-group retail, and gasoline's distortion of the headline.

events.title: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Foundry/AI-cycle bellwether the same week as SEMICON West/ASML; also the silicon-shield read versus gray-zone pressure.
events.what_to_watch: CoWoS/HBM packaging, 2026–27 capex, and China-client scrutiny comments.

events.title: Eurozone September HICP final
events.why_it_matters: Confirms or revises the 3.8% flash that already challenged the ECB's measured hold into Oct 29.
events.what_to_watch: Energy vs core revisions and country dispersion (Germany/Italy).

events.title: CIT briefs in Section 301 forced-labor tariff case
events.why_it_matters: CIT ordered parties to brief statutory authority/remedies on the 12.5% forced-labor 301 layer that sits outside the Busan truce — a binary legal tail on global duties.
events.what_to_watch: Mid-October brief due dates and any hint judges doubt USTR authority.

events.title: US September housing starts and building permits
events.why_it_matters: Rate-sensitive housing vs 10y yields near 24-year highs and $100 oil — a second-order growth/Fed-path print after NFP.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family starts vs permits; August already showed permits 1.394m / starts 1.275m SAAR.

events.title: TRex Bio IPO (Eli Lilly-backed) plus small biotech/SPAC slate
events.why_it_matters: No blockbuster traditional IPO this window; TRex (~$125m) and Retension are a risk-appetite test, not a market-wide event.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the book holds the $14–16 range; larger names (e.g. Anthropic) still later.

events.title: US midterms (Nov 3) enter the four-week stretch
events.why_it_matters: Polls show a large Dem generic-ballot lead and a base case of divided government; Iran/Hormuz decisions are being framed against this clock.
events.what_to_watch: Generic-ballot stability, prediction-market House/Senate odds, and any late-October foreign-policy surprise.

top_risks: Iran/Hormuz kinetic step or another product-side shock while Brent is already ~$101 and diesel is politically painful enough for an EO
Graham Act Oct 8/18 secondary-tariff list hitting China and India, colliding with a still-incomplete USTR implementation of the Jan 10 2027 truce
Hot September CPI headline from gasoline reversing the NFP-driven collapse in October/December hike odds
ISM services prices at 74.0 plus product tightness keeping a stagflation tape even if payrolls stay soft
Long-end yields near 24-year highs tightening financial conditions into bank/UNH earnings regardless of the Fed path
top_opportunities: Soft core CPI (~+0.2% m/m) locking in no October hike and capping December, a risk-on setup for duration-sensitive growth
Samsung (Oct 8) then ASML/TSMC/SEMICON West confirming the AI-memory/WFE boom Micron already printed
China reopen plus Golden Week volume if official spend is less K-shaped than feared
Busan truce + $60bn 30-for-30 lists holding the near-term China tariff cliff through year-end
Divided-government midterm base case (gridlock) if Iran does not force a pre-election shock
summary: The tape is still a two-factor regime: a live US–Iran war with Hormuz restricted, Brent ~$101, and diesel tight enough for a Oct 5 tax-deferral EO, versus a labor-market miss (+29k) that crushed October FOMC hike odds to ~20% ahead of today's minutes. Policy is two-sided — a US–China truce to Jan 10 2027 and $60bn relief lists cut the near-term China tariff cliff, while the Graham Act's Oct 8/18 secondary-tariff clock and a CIT forced-labor 301 briefing keep trade risk binary. Q3 earnings open tomorrow with PepsiCo and Samsung, then banks/UNH/ASML/TSMC against an AI-memory boom Korea and Micron have already validated.
